rv.q: Beetlejuice the musical is louche, macabre and pure, unadulterated fun, full of black-and-white grotesquerie, visual flair and near-the-knuckle jokes.
But this undead scene-stealer stops us from taking the actual narrative here seriously; we don’t have space to feel the aching poignancy just beneath its surface.
But gradually the thin yet complicated plot begins to stall and sag, and the spiky script, ingenious design and sheer gutsy energy of the cast aren’t enough to compensate.
All distract from the carefully designed worlds of the story.
Tightly scripted, tightly choreographed, tightly delivered and for all that, with its great tunes it manages to feel fresh and crisply improvised.
